title: Midweek CSAT touchbase 1-1 - scratch notes (Lena)
content:
Notes to self - quick midweek prep for 1:1 with AE (Marco) on Northwood Retail

Context:
- Account: Northwood Retail (mid-market) — primary use: checkout fraud detection + recommendations pipeline.
- CSAT trend: 4.3 -> 3.9 over last two surveys (decline concentrated in Q4 usage spike).
- Renewal: Jan 2027 (12-month), currently in negotiation window for usage-based clause.
- Last customer touch: 2026-02-12 (QBR with product manager Priya), action: follow up on integration errors and billing spike explanation.

Primary meeting goals (what I want to get out of 1:1):
1) Align AE (Marco) + SE/CS on crisp next steps to diagnose CSAT dip (who owns what, deadlines).
2) Decide whether to open a formal escalation / prioritization with product infra for the integration errors.
3) Draft a short customer-facing plan to re-establish confidence (timeline and milestones we can commit to).

Quick agenda (30 min):
- 0-5 min: quick sync on what Marco heard from customer since QBR (new signals)
- 5-12 min: review usage/billing spike hypothesis (root cause candidates)
- 12-20 min: triage CSAT pain points: latency, billing surprises, missed alerts
- 20-27 min: agree action owners + deadlines; set follow-up cadence
- 27-30 min: prep 1-par email summary for customer + decide if we need to loop ED/PMs

Signals / data points to verify before the call (prep tasks):
- Check billing dashboard for Feb 1-14 token rate (Marco to pull) -> confirm anomaly window.
- Grab latency p95/p99 for recommendation pipeline for same window (SE to confirm).
- Customer reported alerts missed: get alert logs (me) and match to incident IDs.

Hypotheses (for discussion):
- H1: Traffic burst + longer sequences pushed them into fallback model causing higher cost and slower response.
  - Evidence to look for: sudden increase in avg sequence length, model variant in logs, fallbacks recorded in router logs.
- H2: Misconfigured batching on their Dedicated instance after recent release -> higher latency + tokenization mismatch.
- H3: Billing spike due to double-ingest on webhook retry loop (observed pattern for other accounts).

Probing questions to ask Marco (so he can ask customer):
- Since QBR, any changes to traffic patterns (new campaign, product launch, test env left open)?
- Did they change prompt templates or start sending longer contexts?
- Who on their side owns infra (SRE) vs product? Can we get a direct SRE contact?
- Any changes to expected SLA acceptance? Are they pushing for lower latency than contract?

Draft customer-facing lines (keep short / apologetic / factual):
- "We saw a pattern in Feb where your request mix changed; we’re investigating latency and billing signals and will share a short remediation plan by <date>."
- If escalation: "We are opening a priority investigation with our infra team and will provide daily updates until resolved."

Action items (clear owner + due date):
- Marco: confirm whether customer enabled any new experiments (AB tests, dev toggles) and share SRE contact — due 2026-03-02.
- SE (Priya): pull p95/p99 latency and model variant logs for 2026-02-01 -> 2026-02-14; upload snippet to shared folder — due 2026-03-03.
- Lena (me): correlate alert IDs customer shared with our monitoring, draft the first email to customer summarizing findings — due 2026-03-03.
- Infra (if needed): stand up a short trial capture on a mirror stream to reproduce fallback behavior — request to infra by 2026-03-04.
- Billing ops: flag potential duplicate webhook billing pattern and confirm tokenization billing mapping — pinged via JIRA-CC-4521 — due 2026-03-05.

Decision criteria (how we'll decide next steps):
- If latency p99 > 1.5x baseline and matched to model fallback: trigger canary rollback + emergency config tweak.
- If billing shows duplicate ingest: apply billing credit + patch webhook retry logic; escalate to billing ops.
- If customer unhappy after initial fix: propose a short discount and commit specialized SRE hours during the next 30 days.

Risks / unknowns (notes):
- Customer may conflate cost with feature reliability -> need discrete talks for billing vs product.
- If customer SRE is slow to share logs, troubleshooting lag will push timeline.

Follow-up cadence proposal:
- Daily async updates in Slack channel until initial containment (first 72 hrs), then 2x weekly syncs until stable.

Snippets to paste into Slack before 1:1 (quick prompts):
- "Marco — quick ask: can you confirm SRE contact + any infra tickets opened by Northwood since 2/1? I'll bring logs on latency if you have SRE."
- "Priya — can you surface the model variant traces for the spike window so we can see fallbacks?"

Draft short email to customer (first outreach - fill blanks during 1:1):
- Subject: Quick update on Feb performance signals
- Body: "Hi [Name], \n\nThanks again for the QBR — following that, we noticed a performance and billing signal in early Feb that may have impacted your experience. We’re actively investigating (latency, model routing, billing flows) and will share a remediation plan by Friday <date>. Apologies for the disruption — our objective is to get you back to expected levels quickly.\n\nBest,\nLena (on behalf of Redwood CS + Marco)"

Post-meeting checklist (Lena):
- Convert action items into JIRA tasks and assign (do immediately after 1:1).
- Draft customer email and put it in Marco's outbox for approval.
- If infra escalation required, lock a 30-min triage slot with on-call infra.

Open questions to dig into during 1:1 (left unresolved until we have logs):
- Did the customer start hitting a model sequence length cap that triggered different kernel paths?
- Are there any recent changes to their content moderation prompts that could have increased compute?

Random notes / heuristics (personal):
- Keep customer messaging focused and avoid technical jargon unless SRE in thread.
- When offering credits, always quantify benefit (USD amount or % of spike) and attach a short remediation timeline.

End of scratchpad.

TODO (personal quick list):
- 10m pre-call: load billing dashboard and snapshot p95/p99 charts (local).
- 5m pre-call: re-open QBR notes to refresh on decision-makers.
- Immediately after call: create JIRA-CC-4521 sub-tasks and hand off to owners.
